text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Moderate Islamist sect leader Fethullah Gulen, who owns more than 300 schools, also buys well-known Yukselis College in Ankara.
- An expert in social security privatisation in Latin America likens Turkey' social security system to the sunk passenger ship Titanic.
HURRIYET
- A written request for the lifting of the parliamentary immunity of two government MPs implicated in a security scandal has reached parliament after a three-month delay.
MILLIYET
- Police arrest five people for launching armed attack on private television channel Flash TV.
- No money is being spent on the underdeveloped east and southeast of Turkey despite promises by the government.
YENI YUZYIL
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's may threaten to lift the two MPs' parliamentary immunity if coalition partner Tansu Ciller does not stand by him in row with army over religion.
- Economy official Erdal Onurhan says Turkish Cypriots agree in principle to sell port facilities in northern town of Kyrenia to Turkey's Koc Holding in privatisation drive.
RADIKAL
- Turkish armed forces kill 93 Kurdistan Workers Party guerrillas in cross-border operation held in northern Iraq.
- Central Bank governor Gazi Ercel says it necessary to achieve stability in economy and reduce inflation to a one-digit figure if Istanbul wants to become international finance center.
ZAMAN
- State Minister Abdullah Gul says his Islam-based Welfare Party is against plans for uninterrupted eight-year compulsory schooling that would hit religious high schools.
- An official from the prime minister's office says studies are being held to implement mortgage banking in Turkey.
DUNYA
- Authorities will introduce regulations to fight against uninsured workers in the textile business.
